canonical_identity.title: Continuing Appropriations, Agriculture, Legislative Branch, Military Construction and Veterans Affairs, and Extensions Act, 2026

plain_language_description: A government-funding measure whose initial House version provided short-term funding through November 21, 2025 and whose later Senate-amended version ended a shutdown, funded most agencies through January 30, 2026, and enacted three full-year funding divisions.
prior_policy_baseline: FY2026 regular funding bills were unfinished. The initial House vote occurred before the fiscal year began; the later House vote occurred after a funding lapse had run from October 1 through November 11.
proposed_action_or_mechanism: Initial House stage: temporarily continue FY2025 funding and authorities across all 12 annual funding areas. Senate-amended stage: temporarily fund nine areas, provide full-year Agriculture, Legislative Branch, and Military Construction-VA funding, and add extensions and workforce provisions.
directly_affected: States and grantees with covered obligations
implementation_authority: Federal agencies receiving appropriations; Office of Personnel Management and employing agencies for covered workforce provisions.
legislative_history: The House passed the initial version September 19. The Senate later substituted a materially broader package. The House accepted it November 12, and the President signed Public Law 119-37 the same day.

documented_supporter_argument.argument: Supporters of the initial House version argued that it would keep the government operating while appropriators finished annual bills; supporters of the Senate-amended version argued that it would reopen the government, restore services, and enact three negotiated full-year divisions.
documented_supporter_argument.attribution: House floor supporters at the September 19 and November 12 stages
documented_supporter_argument.uncertainty_and_evidence_limits: The two stages had materially different text. This summary preserves both stages and is not attributed to Foushee.

documented_opponent_argument.argument: Opponents of the initial version argued that the short-term bill omitted action on expiring Affordable Care Act premium tax credits; opponents of the final package again objected that it reopened government without extending those credits and raised additional objections to package provisions.
documented_opponent_argument.attribution: House floor opponents at the September 19 and November 12 stages
documented_opponent_argument.uncertainty_and_evidence_limits: The official debate documents arguments made against each stage. It does not establish which objection, if any, explains Foushee's Nay on either roll.

important_uncertainties: The package covered many programs; top-layer copy intentionally names only material stage differences.
A vote on the package does not identify a member's view on every component.
The September and November votes must never share one generic interpretation.
